findings.issue_text: packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:256 — updateEvent`'s fallback branch computes `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` but this code path only runs when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, so it searches the array for an entry whose externalId equals a falsy value — effectively always `undefined` — silently discarding the previous behavior of falling back to the event's own destination calendar and causing the Google API call to run with `calendarId: undefined`.

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:317 — Same broken fallback pattern in `deleteEvent`: `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` compares against the falsy `externalCalendarId` that triggered this branch, so it never finds a match and `calendarId` silently falls back to `"primary"`, meaning delete-by-destination-calendar is effectively broken and could delete/attempt-delete against the wrong (primary) calendar.

goldens.comment: A null reference occurs in GoogleCalendarService.createEvent() and updateEvent() when mainHostDestinationCalendar is destructured from evt.destinationCalendar but evt.destinationCalendar is null or an empty array, causing mainHostDestinationCalendar to be undefined.
The optional chaining on mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration is redundant since you already check mainHostDestinationCalendar in the ternary condition.

Logic error: when externalCalendarId is provided, you're searching for a calendar where externalId === externalCalendarId, but this will always fail since you're looking for a calendar that matches itself. Should likely find by credentialId or use different logic.

Logic inversion in organization creation: The slug property is now conditionally set when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true, instead of when it's false as originally intended. This change, combined with requestedSlug still being set when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true, results in both properties being set when billing is enabled, and neither when disabled

The Calendar interface now requires createEvent(event, credentialId), but some implementations (e.g., Lark/Office365) still declare createEvent(event) only—this breaks the interface contract (also applies to other locations in the PR).

The `credential` may be undefined when passed to `updateEvent` if `reference.credentialId` is set but the credential is not found. This can lead to a runtime error when `updateEvent` is called with an undefined credential, which should be handled to prevent crashes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:256 — updateEvent`'s fallback branch computes `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` but this code path only runs when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, so it searches the array for an entry whose externalId equals a falsy value — effectively always `undefined` — silently discarding the previous behavior of falling back to the event's own destination calendar and causing the Google API call to run with `calendarId: undefined`.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` the new `updateEvent` fallback changed from `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId` (old single object) to `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`. But this fallback branch is only taken when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, so it searches for a destination calendar whose `externalId` equals a falsy value (typically `undefined`/`null`), which will almost always return `undefined`. This silently drops the intended fallback-to-event-destination-calendar behavior and can lead to `selectedCalendar` being undefined (and thus the Google API call using an incorrect/undefined calendarId or falling back to default elsewhere, changing behavior).

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:317 — Same broken fallback pattern in `deleteEvent`: `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` compares against the falsy `externalCalendarId` that triggered this branch, so it never finds a match and `calendarId` silently falls back to `"primary"`, meaning delete-by-destination-calendar is effectively broken and could delete/attempt-delete against the wrong (primary) calendar.

adjudication.rationale:
The diff changes `deleteEvent` (and similarly `updateEvent`) to compute `calendarId` as:

```ts
const calendarId = externalCalendarId
  ? externalCalendarId
  : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;
```

In the `else` branch, `externalCalendarId` is falsy (that’s why the branch is taken), so the `.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` compares against `undefined`/`null` and will not match any real destination calendar externalId. That makes `calendarId` become `undefined`, and the subsequent code falls back to the default (`"primary"`). This is a concrete logic bug introduced by the diff: when `externalCalendarId` is not provided, it will never select a destination calendar from `event.destinationCalendar` and will instead operate on the primary calendar (likely failing or targeting the wrong calendar).
